title: Expected Additional Property Tax Collections Following November 2023 Announcement of Increase
what_it_is: Expected Additional Property Tax Collections Following November 2023 Announcement of Increase

sections.label: Property tax and AV increases
sections.summary: Most owner-occupied homes saw AV rise over 20% in 2024, and property tax rates rose in 2023 and 2024 for high-value and non-owner-occupied properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For 2024, most owner-occupied residential properties saw their AV increase by more than 20% due to the increase in market rentals from 2022 to 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: In addition, as announced in Budget 2022 as a form of wealth tax, property tax rates were increased in two steps in 2023 and 2024, for high-value owner-occupied private properties with AVs above $30,000, as well as all non-owner-occupied properties.

sections.label: Property tax rebate and revenue
sections.summary: Government gave rebates up to 100% capped at $1,000, and 2024 residential property tax revenue is expected around $600 million higher than 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Two, to cushion the impact of the increase on owner-occupiers, the Government has provided a property tax rebate of up to 100%, capped at $1,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: With the rebate, owner-occupiers of Housing and Development Board (HDB) 1- and 2-room flats continue to pay no property tax; for owner-occupiers of other HDB flat types, the average property tax increase is less than $3 per month; and for half of private property owner-occupiers, their increase in property tax was less than $15 per month.

On Mr Pritam Singh's query on property tax collections, after accounting for the 2024 property tax rebate, the 2024 residential property tax revenue is expected to be around $600 million higher than the 2023 PT collections.
Around two-thirds of the increase is contributed by non-owner-occupied properties.

sections.label: Request to review tax increase
sections.summary: A Member asks whether MOF will review the hefty tax increase on owner-occupied properties and consider a higher rebate than the $1,000 cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, the impact of the increase in property tax on them is actually quite high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, may I ask the Minister whether the Ministry of Finance (MOF) will consider reviewing the hefty tax increase on owner-occupied properties and, perhaps, consider a higher amount of rebate, rather than have it capped at $1,000?

sections.label: Considering more property tax help
sections.summary: The Minister says the Government is prepared to consider more help, and that after the 15% rebate capped at $1,000, half of private owner-occupiers face increases under $15 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: To the point about whether we can provide more help through property tax rebates, this is something which, in my main reply, I said, Ms Joan Pereira had also asked, we are prepared to consider and to take a look and see what we can do to help, not just seniors but also other families who are facing a large increase in their property tax bills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: While it is true that some households may face a higher increase, depending on the AV of the property, because the larger the property, the higher the AV, the larger the magnitude of the increase would be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But, if we look at private properties across the board and, after the rebate – the 15% rebate capped at $1,000 – half of private property owner-occupiers will see their property tax payable increase by less than $15 per month.

sections.label: Objecting to property AV
sections.summary: Owners can provide grounds of objection with evidence, and if unsatisfied, appeal to the Valuation Review Board within 30 days of IRAS' decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: They can provide the grounds of objection, including evidence to support the different AV.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And, if they are not satisfied with the outcome of the objection, they can appeal to the Valuation Review Board within 30 days of IRAS' decision.

sections.label: Ad hoc assistance questioned
sections.summary: A Member says instead of ad hoc assistance, he does not know what the Minister alluded to about IRAS possibly providing assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Instead of ad hoc assistance, I do not know what the Minister was alluding to when he said that IRAS may look into providing assistance.
